headline: Eight categories, four verdicts. Only TWO are worth the product's time: WEATHER (176) is the most modellable non-sport on the book - it settles on observed air temperature at named international airports at a stated UTC instant, and both a free keyless forecast API and a free machine-readable settlement feed are verified; and POLITICS (202) is priced at 6.7-8.3% overround, at or BELOW the book's own 7.14% football median, on real elections with real public signal - blocked not by modelling but by a jurisdictional-legality question. LOTTERY (82) is RNG and unmodellable by construction. TOTO (69) is a bet on Betwinner's OWN pool whose decisive input (the crowd's entry distribution) is never published. SPECIAL BETS (87) is a bag of n=1 novelties with no reference class. TV GAMES (20) is NOT the casino RNG vertical of the same name - it is an awards/TV-outright book, forecastable in principle but priced at 20-30% hold. GAMES OF THE FUTURE (303) IS the real Kazan-lineage phygital tournament, 2026 edition in Astana - real, but with no results feed and only 2 markets a match. POLYBET (314) is a Polymarket-shaped real-world event book of 1584 events priced at 0.80% overround on crypto - and it is the one place in the entire book where CLAUDE.md's 'there is no reference book' premise is FALSE.
method: Every category fact below is read from Betwinner's OWN LineFeed, pulled live from this machine on 2026-07-25 (betwinner.com/service-api/LineFeed, partner=159, no key, HTTP 200): GetSportsShortZip for the catalogue, GetChampsZip per sportId for tournaments, Get1x2_VZip per tournament for events, GetGameZip (countevents=5000) per event for the priced selections. Nothing about what a category 'is' was inferred from the label alone - the tournament and event names are quoted from the payload. Overrounds are computed by grouping selections on (G, GS, P, PL) - the actual market key - and summing 1/odds; grouping on (G, GS) alone produces fake 100-500% figures because this feed bundles independent propositions under one group id (see key_findings).

categories.name: TV Games
categories.what_it_is: NOT the 1xBet/Betwinner casino vertical of the same name (the presenter-hosted RNG wheel/keno/bingo titles). LineFeed sportId 20 is an ENTERTAINMENT OUTRIGHT book: 64 events across 15 tournaments, all quoted live from the feed - Emmy Award 2026, Hugo Award 2026 (Best Novel), Logie Awards 2026 (Gold Logie), Nobel Peace Prize 2026, Grammy 2027 (Album of the Year), Academy Awards 2027 (Best Actor/Actress/Picture/Most Nominations, venue MIO.Loc = 'Dolby Theatre (Los Angeles)'), Triple J Hottest 100 2026, Coachella 2027 headliner, Birgit Nilsson Prize 2028, TV-Shows Great Britain (Strictly Come Dancing 2026 winner), TV-Shows Italy (X Factor 2026 winner's mentor / winning category), TV-Shows USA (60 Minutes specials, Netflix Roast next athlete), Special bets Cinema (Highest Grossing Film of 2026, Biggest USA Domestic Opening Weekend), Special bets Music (Rolling Stone #1 Album/Song, Spotify Wrapped Top Global Artist), Special bets Awards (Time Person of the Year, People Sexiest Man Alive, BBC Sports Personality). The name collision with the casino product is the single most likely source of a wrong call on this id, and it resolves the wrong way from the label alone.
categories.modellable_detail: Real-world in the strict sense - juried and voted human decisions, no RNG. Award races are genuinely forecastable in the literature (precursor/guild awards, critics' aggregates, nomination counts). But for THIS product: one observation per market per year, no repeated trials, no reference class the scanner can build, no results loop, and a live information-asymmetry risk (embargoed results, production staff, pre-recorded reality formats where the outcome already exists before the market closes). A sub-segment is effectively scripted rather than competitive.
categories.measured_overround: Emmy Outstanding Comedy Series, 8 runners, +30.2%. Emmy Outstanding Drama Series, 8 runners, +28.3%. Emmy Lead Actor in a Comedy Series, 5 runners, +20.0%. Against the 7.14% median football hold this project measured, that is 3-4x the price of the core book.
categories.recommendation: EXCLUDE from ranking. At 20-30% hold with n=1 events and no feedback loop there is nothing the scanner can honestly say about these. If the operator wants them visible, surface them in a separate tab labelled 'novelty - unmodelled, hold 20-30%' and keep them out of the top-50 and out of any parlay.

categories.name: Toto
categories.what_it_is: NOT a match market and not a Toto entry. The single tournament is 'TOTO total betting results' (feed RU label: 'Ставки на результаты тотализатора ТОТО' - bets ON the results of the TOTO totalizator). These are bets on the AGGREGATE OUTCOME OF BETWINNER'S OWN PARIMUTUEL POOL. 4 draws live: Toto Fifteen Draw No.4257 (15-match football pool), Toto Football Draw No.1133, Toto correct score Draw No.4268, Toto Cyber football Draw No.26693. Market structure decoded from GetGameZip: outcome types T12014 / T12015 are an Over / Under pair on P = 11,12,13,14,15 - i.e. over/under the number of correctly predicted outcomes achieved in that pool draw. Feed field TN = 'draw'.
categories.outcome_source_detail: MIXED, and the mix matters. Toto Fifteen and Toto Football rest on real football matches. Toto CYBER football (Draw No.26693) rests on SIMULATED football - engine/RNG-driven virtual matches, not a real fixture list. One of the four live draws is therefore RNG at its base.
categories.modellable_detail: The quantity being priced is max-correct-predictions across the pool's entrants. That is a function of (a) the per-match outcome probabilities, which we could estimate, AND (b) the joint distribution of what the ENTRANTS picked, which Betwinner does not publish. (b) dominates: a pool where everyone picks the favourites produces a very different max-correct than one with dispersed entries, at identical match probabilities. The decisive input is structurally unobservable. This is not a data gap we can close by finding a better source - the book is the only holder of it.
categories.measured_overround: Two-way lines: O/U 13 correct = +8.1%, O/U 14 = +11.7%. The outer lines are dead - the under side prices at 1.001, the feed's placeholder value (O/U 11 and O/U 12 both carry 1.001).
categories.recommendation: EXCLUDE entirely. The book has private information that is the single largest term in the model, one of the four draws is a virtual-football sim, and half the priced lines are 1.001 placeholders that would need suppressing anyway.

categories.name: Lottery
categories.what_it_is: Number betting on real, licensed lottery draws - 319 events across 54 tournaments in 12 countries/regions, all quoted from the feed: Europe EuroJackpot and EuroMillions 5/50; USA MegaMillions, California Daily3 3/10, Daily4 4/10, Fantasy 5 5/39, Florida PICK-3, PICK-4, Fantasy 5 (Midday and Evening variants); United Kingdom 49's 6/49; Germany LOTTO 6/49 and KENO 20/70; Spain La Primitiva 6/49; Austria LOTTO 6/45; Belgium KENO 20/70 and PICK-3; Canada LOTTO 6/49, BC 49, Ontario KENO and PICK-3 (Midday/Evening); Australia Oz Lotto and Tattslotto; Ukraine SUPER LOTO 6/52, LOTO MAXIMA 5/45, LOTO TRIYKA 3/10, KENO 20/80; Belarus Sportloto 5/36 and 6/49; Russia Rapido Drive/Pro/Ultra, Big 8, Magnificent 8, All or nothing 12/24, KENO 20/80, Sportloto 4/20. Betwinner is not selling tickets - it is pricing derivative propositions ON the draw: sum over/under, odd/even counts, ball ranges, colour. Depth is enormous: MegaMillions alone returned 482 distinct two-way markets / 991 selections in a single draw, UK 49's 170 markets.
categories.modellable_detail: UNMODELLABLE BY CONSTRUCTION, and it is worth being precise about why, because the usual phrasing is slightly wrong. It is not that we cannot compute the probabilities - we can compute them EXACTLY. The true probability of every one of these derivative markets is a closed-form or trivially enumerable combinatorial quantity (P(sum of 6 drawn from 49 exceeds 150) is an exact number, not an estimate). What is missing is not model skill but INFORMATION ASYMMETRY. Past draws carry literally zero information about future ones; the exact fair price is known to us and to the book identically; the book prices above it; therefore no edge can exist. Physical ball draws and certified RNG are informationally identical here.
categories.measured_overround: 3.10-3.11%, measured as the median over 482 two-way MegaMillions markets and 170 two-way UK 49's markets. That is LESS THAN HALF the 7.14% median football hold this project measured.
categories.recommendation: EXCLUDE entirely, and do it EXPLICITLY in config rather than trusting the filters - see key_findings[0]. At 3.1% these markets are the cheapest in the book by a wide margin, so a margin-normalised ranker will place them at the top of every single run. NARROW LEGITIMATE USE, if the operator wants one: because the exact fair probability is computable, sport 82 is the only place in the book where the TRUE hold can be measured exactly instead of estimated by proportional de-vig. It is a calibration bench for engine/score.py, not a betting surface. Nothing from it should ever reach the top-50 or a parlay.

categories.name: Special Bets
categories.what_it_is: 23 events across 7 tournaments, quoted from the feed: 'Game of Thrones. "The Winds of Winter". Special Bets' (publication of an unwritten novel), 'Space. Specials', 'Special bets' (which contains Robert Irwin specials, USA Donald Trump specials, GTA VI launch postponement), 'Sperm Racing Cup. 2026. Special bets', 'Taylor Swift. Special bets', 'The Professional Bull Riders', and "World's Most Livable City. 2027". Structurally most of these are group 9242/3042 BUNDLES of independent Yes/No propositions listed under one event heading, not exclusive markets - e.g. 'Robert Irwin. Special bets' lists 15 unrelated props (Instagram follower count, Masked Singer appearance, TIME cover, Hot Ones guest).
categories.modellable_detail: Real-world but n=1 with no reference class. 'Will George R. R. Martin publish The Winds of Winter' has no base rate; 'Donald Trump to add himself to Mt. Rushmore' has no base rate; there is no repeated trial, no results loop, and no free data source that would inform any of them. One genuine exception is mis-filed: The Professional Bull Riders is a real professional sport with real riders and real historical results - it does not belong in a novelty bucket and should be re-homed to a sport model if the book keeps listing it here.
categories.measured_overround: Not meaningfully computable for the bundles, and this is itself the finding: summing a 9242/3042 bundle gives +158.7% (Robert Irwin, 15 props) and +168.5% (Trump specials, 5 props), which are artefacts of adding up independent propositions, not holds. The one genuine two-way found - 'GTA VI Launch to be Postponed Again' - prices at +6.2%.
categories.recommendation: EXCLUDE entirely. Flag The Professional Bull Riders for re-homing. Also flag this category to the engine as a de-vig hazard: it is the clearest example of a bundle that must never be treated as an exclusive market.

categories.name: Weather
categories.what_it_is: One tournament, 'Weather in the Airports of the world', 80 events (50 returned in one pull) spanning 20 world regions - Australia and New Zealand, Caribbean, Central/East/North/West Africa, Central America, Central Asia, East Asia, Eastern/Northern/Southern/Western Europe, Melanesia, North/South America, Polynesia, South Asia, South-East Asia, West Asia. Each EVENT is one settlement instant in UTC (observed: '28/07/2026 00:00:00 UTC'), and the participants (feed field PL) are NAMED INTERNATIONAL AIRPORTS with stable ids: Auckland International Airport, Sydney Kingsford Smith, Warsaw Chopin, Sheremetyevo, Minsk International, Ostrava Leos Janacek, Toronto Lester B. Pearson, Bermuda L.F. Wade. Two outcome types are used. T13117 carries a P that encodes an INCLUSIVE DEGREE BAND as A.0BB - 4.009 is 4-9 C, 15.021 is 15-21 C, 10.011 is 10-11 C. T13118 carries a P that is a single integer degree. Per airport the two tile the Celsius axis contiguously and without gaps - verified independently on 8 airports across 4 regions (e.g. Warsaw: bands [4-9],[10-11] then singles 12,13,14 then bands [15-16],[17-23]; Toronto: [15-21],[22-23], singles 24,25, then [26-27],[28-32],[33-36]).
categories.modellable_detail: THE most modellable category on this list, and the only one where the whole chain is free and verified. The settlement variable is air temperature at a fixed WMO/ICAO station at a fixed instant - a public, numerically forecastable physical observable with well-characterised skill at the 24-72h leads the book is pricing. A free keyless forecast API returns hourly air_temperature for arbitrary coordinates (MET Norway, verified below, 40,066 bytes for Warsaw Chopin), and a free keyless observation API returns the settling integer-Celsius METAR value for exactly these ICAO stations (aviationweather.gov, verified below - EPWA 17 C, UUEE 14 C, NZAA 10 C, YSSY 10 C at 2026-07-25T21:30Z). Betwinner's bands are integer Celsius; METAR temperature is reported in integer Celsius; the units line up without conversion loss.
categories.measured_overround: NOT COMPUTABLE from the feed, and this is an unresolved blocker rather than a result - see open_questions[0]. Every weather selection is returned one-sided: the market key (G=10205, GS=4116, P, PL) has exactly one row, with no opposite side. Summing the contiguous tiling per airport gives 2.66-2.77 in implied probability, which is not a coherent single-market overround, and at least some listed prices are not real (Bermuda 'exactly 27' at 1.016 = 98.4% implied is impossible as a single-degree price; the outermost band of every airport prices at exactly 5.000, which looks like a cap).
categories.recommendation: INCLUDE AND MODEL - the only category here that earns it - but gate it on resolving the market semantics first. The modelling case is unambiguous and the data is verified free on both ends. What is NOT yet known is whether the book's price is worth taking, because we cannot compute the hold until we know what T13117/T13118 actually mean and which listed prices are live. Do not wire margin_score for sport 176 until that is answered; margin_score is undefined for a one-sided feed.

categories.name: Politics
categories.what_it_is: 157 events across 14 country tournaments. Genuine elections dominate, all quoted from the feed: USA (2026 Senate primaries - Michigan Democratic, Virginia Republican; Congress specials), Great Britain (Clacton constituency by-election - winner, percentage of votes, specials; Greater Manchester Mayor 2026; General Election Most Seats), Sweden (Sept 2026 general - most seats, highest percentage of votes, candidate to be appointed PM), France (2027 Presidential - winner and specials), Ireland (parliamentary, most seats), Israel (next PM after election; Netanyahu specials), New Zealand (Nov 2026 general - winner), Canada (Toronto and Ottawa municipal elections, Oct 2026), Poland, Brazil, Australia (federal by-election Secret Harbour; next One Nation leader), European Union, and Politics.Special (next UN Secretary-General after Guterres). A minority of the events are novelty rather than electoral ('Holiday that Donald Trump will cancel first') and should be split out.
categories.modellable_detail: Real elections with real public signal: opinion polling, prior constituency/national results, incumbency and swing, and - decisively for this product - a liquid free public prediction market (Polymarket, verified below; 51 of the 60 highest-volume live markets are election-related). Settlement is an official electoral-commission count, which is a hard, published, auditable number, unlike anything in categories 20/87. The modelling obstacle is not conceptual, it is that we have not yet verified a free polling ingest for the specific races the book lists - see blocked[] for the Swedish and UK gaps, which bite hardest because Sweden votes in September 2026 and Clacton in August 2026.
categories.measured_overround: Michigan Democratic Primary winner (2-way) +6.7%. Clacton by-election winner (2-way) +7.0%. Greater Manchester Mayor 2026 (6-way) +8.3%. That is at or below the 7.14% median football hold this project measured - politics is among the cheapest genuinely modellable product on the entire book. Note the 'Special bets' events in the same tournaments are bundles and price at +115.2% when naively summed; they must be separated from the electoral markets.
categories.legal_note: THIS IS THE ONE CATEGORY HERE WITH A DISTINCT LEGAL PROFILE BEYOND THE GENERAL OFFSHORE-BOOK PROBLEM ALREADY RECORDED IN PRODUCT_STATUS.md. Betting on elections and political outcomes is restricted or prohibited in a number of jurisdictions, and the restrictions attach to the SUBJECT MATTER, not merely to the operator's licence - so 'the book is offshore anyway' does not dispose of it. Several regulated markets bar political betting outright or licence it only under specific conditions, and the US position on election event contracts has been actively litigated rather than settled. Whether a tool that SURFACES (rather than places) a political market carries exposure is a legal question, not an engineering one. Recorded, not resolved - the same treatment PRODUCT_STATUS.md gives the jurisdiction risk. Get an answer before this ships to anyone but the operator.
categories.recommendation: INCLUDE BUT LABEL UNMODELLED, pending two gates. Technically it is the strongest non-weather case on the list and it is cheap. But (1) the legal question above must be answered before a prediction product surfaces political markets to users, and (2) no free polling ingest is yet verified for the live races. Until both clear, carry politics with a visible 'unmodelled' label and no ladder/parlay participation. Split the 'Special bets' bundle events out of the category before any de-vig touches it.

categories.name: Games of the Future
categories.what_it_is: CONFIRMED as the real televised phygital tournament - the operator's hypothesis is correct. Wikipedia REST summary (verified, HTTP 200): 'The Games of the Future is an annual global phygital sports tournament, organized by Phygital International.' The inaugural 2024 edition was in Kazan; the Betwinner feed's 2026 events are staged at 'SK Qazaqstan (Astana)' (feed field MIO.Loc), corroborated independently by phygitalinternational.com, whose homepage carries 20 occurrences of 'Astana' alongside 2026 and both discipline names. 16 events across 2 tournaments: 'Phygital Basketball. Games of the Future. 2026' and 'Phygital Football. Games of the Future. 2026', first fixtures 2026-07-29, with real named club teams - GTB KZ, Zagrebacki malisani NITUI, Vozdovac Beograd, MINSK, LIGA PRO TEAM, Team Apex, Flow Game Basketball, Triada, Dangerous, HandsomeMDMX. This is NOT a virtual/simulated product and must not be confused with the book's Cyber/virtual sports or with the Toto Cyber football draw.
categories.modellable_detail: Real head-to-head competition between real athletes, so modellable in principle - but not in practice today, for three concrete reasons. (1) NO RESULTS FEED: both official sites are robots-clean and reachable (gamesofthefuture.com 200/45,838 bytes; phygitalinternational.com 200/280,520 bytes) but neither carries any results, standings or schedule content - zero occurrences of those terms in either body. Without settled results there is no rating, no backtest, nothing. (2) THIN MARKET: only 2 markets per match - a moneyline and one total (e.g. total points 61.5 for phygital basketball) - so there is nothing to rank within a match. (3) HYBRID RULES: a phygital score combines a video-game leg and a physical leg, which invalidates conventional basketball/football scoring priors; you cannot borrow a basketball total model for a 61.5-point phygital total.
categories.measured_overround: +9.0% to +9.3% across 6 two-way markets (moneyline and total). Priced like a normal minor sport - the book is not treating this as a novelty.
categories.recommendation: INCLUDE BUT LABEL UNMODELLED. It is a real sport, priced like a real sport, and it deserves to be in the universe rather than filtered out by reflex - the operator's instruction is exactly right here. But with no results feed and 2 markets a match it cannot carry a model or a ladder today. Re-check after the 2026 edition completes: if Phygital International publishes results, this becomes an ordinary small-sport modelling problem.

categories.name: Polybet
categories.what_it_is: The largest category on this list by an order of magnitude - 1584 events across 65 tournaments - and a Polymarket-shaped real-world event book, which is what the name is telling you. Tournaments quoted from the feed: App Store (#1 Free/Paid app in the US App Store on a named date), Apple (iPhone 18 release, foldable iPhone, Vision Pro 2), Artificial intelligence (Moonshot to publish Kimi K3 weights by July 27; company with the #2/#3 AI model end of July, Style Control On - i.e. leaderboard positions), Business (S&P Global Q2 rating revenues, Coca-Cola Q2 organic revenue growth, Amphenol Q2 organic sales, Corning optical sales - real corporate earnings lines), Celebrities, Climate (precipitation in London/New York/Hong Kong/Seoul in July; July temperature-record placing), Cryptocurrency (what price Bitcoin/Ethereum/Dogecoin/Chainlink will hit in July 2026; MicroStrategy BTC sale announcements), Economy (Fed decision July 2026, number of dissents at the July FOMC, Bank of England July decision, US Q2 GDP growth), Elon Musk, Emmy Awards, Eurovision (2027 host city, participants), Google (#1 searched person/actor), Medicine (FDA approvals for Retatrutide and Daraxonrasib, CDC Level 4 warning, US cyclosporiasis cases), Movies (box office weekends, Netflix weekly charts, San Diego Comic-Con), Music, and roughly 45 country-politics sub-books (Albania, Argentina, Bosnia, Brazil, Bulgaria, Canada, China, Cook Islands, DR Congo, ...).
categories.modellable_detail: Partially, and this is the most interesting case here. The macro and financial subsets have genuine public inputs: Fed decisions have published market-implied probabilities and a dot plot, GDP has nowcasts, corporate earnings lines have analyst consensus, crypto price levels have live spot and options-implied distributions. Crucially, a large share of these questions map ONE-TO-ONE onto Polymarket questions where a liquid public price already exists and is free to read (verified below). The celebrity/novelty subset (Obamas to divorce, Bieber split) is n=1 with no reference class and is not modellable, exactly like sport 87.
categories.measured_overround: Cryptocurrency price markets: +0.80% median over 27 two-way markets. Economy: bimodal, +0.80% on some Fed lines and +5.0% on others (number of dissents at the July FOMC prices at +5.0%). Single event props like 'MicroStrategy to announce selling any Bitcoin July 21-27' price at +5.1%. A 0.80% two-way overround is thinner than ANY sports market this project has measured and thinner than the lottery's 3.1%. A bookmaker does not set a 0.80% margin from its own opinion; it is what mirroring an external market at a hair of markup looks like.
categories.recommendation: INCLUDE AND MODEL - but as a REFERENCE-PRICE COMPARISON (Betwinner vs Polymarket on matched questions), NOT as a within-book cheapness rank. This is the one category that breaks the project's founding premise: CLAUDE.md says 'There is no reference book', and for Polybet that is simply false - Polymarket publishes a free, keyless, liquid price for a large share of these exact questions, verified below. That changes what the product can honestly claim here from 'ranks within Betwinner's own prices' to an actual two-source comparison. Two cautions. (1) At 0.80% hold the book has almost no cushion, which in practice means low limits and fast line movement - and Betwinner publishes no limits, so we cannot see it. (2) margin_score would rank every Polybet crypto market above everything else in the book for the same mechanical reason lottery does; sport 314 must be handled outside the standard margin normalisation, not merged into it.

verified.coverage: The book's own pre-match feed, reachable from THIS machine (unlike betwinner.com's web pages, which 302 to betwinner2.com). Every category fact in this file is read from it. Confirmed live event counts per sportId on 2026-07-25: 20=64 events/15 tournaments, 69=4/1, 82=319/54, 87=23/7, 176=80/1, 202=157/14, 303=16/2, 314=1584/65. Endpoints used: GetSportsShortZip, GetChampsZip, Get1x2_VZip, GetGameZip (countevents=5000).
verified.note: Grouped tournaments hide their real sub-tournaments in the SC array (Lottery uses this heavily - 'Australia', 'Russia', 'USA' are group nodes, the actual draws are underneath). Descending into SC is mandatory or whole countries go missing, which tools/fetch_window.py already handles. No 'limit' field anywhere in these categories, consistent with the rest of the book.

verified.coverage: HTTP 200, 40,066 bytes of real JSON for Warsaw Chopin. Global hourly forecast at arbitrary coordinates. Body confirmed to contain: properties.meta.updated_at '2026-07-25T19:17:40Z', units block declaring air_temperature in celsius, and a timeseries of instant.details carrying air_temperature (17.4 at 21:00Z, 16.8 at 22:00Z), air_pressure_at_sea_level, relative_humidity, cloud_area_fraction, wind_from_direction, wind_speed, plus next_1_hours/next_6_hours/next_12_hours precipitation_amount and symbol_code. This is a directly usable model input for Betwinner sportId 176.
verified.note: ROBOTS-CLEAN FOR US: api.met.no/robots.txt reads 'User-agent: Googlebot / User-agent: AdsBot-Google / Allow: /*/documentation / Disallow: /weatherapi/*' and then 'User-agent: * / Disallow:' - the /weatherapi/ block applies ONLY to the two Google agents; the wildcard group has an EMPTY Disallow, which means allow-all. We are in the wildcard group. MET Norway's terms require an identifying User-Agent with a contact address (sent: 'ClaudeBot/1.0 betwinner-odds-research (trz.ahmet@gmail.com)') and rate-limiting; data is NLOD/CC-BY. This is the robots-clean substitute for Open-Meteo - see blocked[open_meteo_api].

verified.coverage: HTTP 200, 1,655 bytes of real JSON. THE SETTLEMENT QUANTITY for sportId 176. Returns per ICAO station: temp (integer C), dewp, wdir, wspd, visib, altim, obsTime/reportTime, the rawOb METAR string, and lat/lon/elev/name. Live values read 2026-07-25T21:30Z: EPWA 'Warsaw/Chopin Arpt, MZ, PL' temp 17 (rawOb 'METAR EPWA 252130Z 16006KT CAVOK 17/12 Q1008 NOSIG'); UUEE 'Moscow/Sheremetyevo Intl' temp 14; NZAA 'Auckland Intl' temp 10; YSSY 'Sydney' temp 10. Every airport Betwinner names in sportId 176 is an ICAO station this API serves, and the integer-Celsius reporting matches the book's integer bands with no conversion loss.
verified.note: aviationweather.gov serves NO robots.txt (HTTP 404, nginx) - no directives, nothing to violate. US NOAA Aviation Weather Center, public-domain data. Pairs with metno_locationforecast to close BOTH ends of the weather chain: forecast in, observed settlement out. Getting the observed side free is what makes a results loop possible for sport 176 - which is the P0 gap PRODUCT_STATUS.md names for every other sport.

verified.coverage: HTTP 200, 19,259 bytes of real JSON. Live prediction-market prices, no key. 51 of the 60 highest-volume open markets are election/politics-related (2028 US presidential and party nominations, next PM of Ethiopia, etc.). Fields confirmed present in the body: question, conditionId, slug, resolutionSource, description, endDate, startDate, outcomes, outcomePrices, volume, liquidity, active, closed, umaResolutionStatus. Example row read live: 'Will Jesus Christ return before 2027?' outcomes [Yes,No], outcomePrices [0.0195, 0.9805], volume 64,830,650, liquidity 954,878.
verified.note: DIRECTLY RELEVANT TO SPORTS 202 AND 314 - this is a genuine free public REFERENCE price for the same real-world questions Betwinner prices, which the project does not have for any sport. robots: polymarket.com/robots.txt is 'User-agent: *' plus a Sitemap line and NO Disallow; the gamma-api host serves no robots.txt (404). outcomePrices are already probabilities (they sum to ~1.0), so no de-vig is needed on this side. Caveat before relying on it: an unmatched question is worse than no reference, so a name/semantics matching pass is required - see open_questions.

verified.coverage: HTTP 200, 1,806 bytes JSON. Used to independently confirm what sportId 303 is: extract reads 'The Games of the Future is an annual global phygital sports tournament, organized by Phygital International.' wikibase_item Q124658566. No '2026_Games_of_the_Future' page exists yet (404 on that title), so the 2026 Astana venue rests on the Betwinner feed's MIO.Loc plus phygitalinternational.com, not on Wikipedia.
verified.note: en.wikipedia.org/robots.txt returned HTTP 403 with an 82-byte body 'Too many requests. Please contact bot-traffic@wikimedia.org to discuss unblocking.' on one attempt from this egress and HTTP 200 (28,275 bytes, the normal permissive file) minutes later. That is RATE-LIMITING on our shared egress IP, not a disallow - back off and retry rather than recording it as blocked. Worth knowing because the same pattern will look like a block in CI.

verified.coverage: HTTP 200, 280,520 bytes of real HTML. Confirms the 2026 edition and its location - 20 occurrences of 'Astana', 69 of '2026', and both 'phygital basketball' and 'Phygital Football', corroborating the Betwinner feed's MIO.Loc 'SK Qazaqstan (Astana)'. NEGATIVE COVERAGE FINDING, which is the more important half: ZERO occurrences of 'result', 'schedule' or 'standings' anywhere in the body. The organiser's own site publishes no results feed.
verified.note: robots.txt is 'User-agent: * / Disallow:' (allow-all, Yoast block) - clean. Same for gamesofthefuture.com ('User-agent: * / Disallow:', HTTP 200, 45,838 bytes) which is even thinner: zero occurrences of 'Astana', 'result', 'schedule' or 'standings'. Verified reachable and verified USELESS for modelling - this is why sportId 303 is 'include but label unmodelled' rather than 'include and model'.

verified.coverage: HTTP 200, 29,631 bytes of real HTML (dcterms.issued 2026-07-09, dcterms.creator 'Elections Canada'). Official federal settlement source. robots.txt permits us: the wildcard group is 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /pol/can/sof/efr/' - one path only, unrelated to results.
verified.note: PARTIAL FIT ONLY, stated plainly: Betwinner's live Canadian politics markets are the Toronto and Ottawa MUNICIPAL elections (Oct 2026), which Elections Canada does not run - municipal results come from the cities themselves. Elections Canada settles federal races, which are not currently on the book. Recorded as a verified source with a coverage mismatch rather than a solution.

blocked.detail: NOT FETCHED - ROBOTS-DISALLOWED, and this is the finding the operator should look at hardest because Open-Meteo is the obvious first choice. https://api.open-meteo.com/robots.txt returns HTTP 200 with a body of exactly 'User-agent: *' / 'Disallow: /'. We are covered by the wildcard, so under this project's stated compliance policy the API host was not called. Note the split within the same brand: the DOCUMENTATION site https://open-meteo.com/robots.txt returns 'User-agent: *' / 'Allow: /' - docs readable, API host not. OPERATOR DECISION, not an engineering one: this is a blanket anti-crawler directive sitting on an API host whose entire product IS programmatic access, and the identical pattern appears on the US National Weather Service's own public API (https://api.weather.gov/robots.txt is also exactly 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /'). If the operator reads robots.txt as governing crawlers rather than documented API clients, Open-Meteo and api.weather.gov both become available. Until that call is made, api.met.no is the robots-clean equivalent and was used instead - it returns the same air_temperature quantity and is verified above, so NOTHING is lost on the weather chain by respecting this.

ROBOTS-DISALLOWED BY NAME - NOT FETCHED. https://www.electionguide.org/robots.txt contains the literal consecutive lines 'User-agent: ClaudeBot' then 'Disallow: /'. We are named, so the IFES election calendar is off-limits regardless of what it would return. Independently confirmed to be WAF-blocked as well: the site returned HTTP 403 with a 25-byte body 'Your request was blocked.' The robots file also carries a Cloudflare content-signals preamble ('If a Content-Signal = no, you may not collect content for the corresponding use').

WAF-BLOCKED, NOT ROBOTS-BLOCKED - the distinction matters for retry strategy. https://www.electoralcommission.org.uk/robots.txt is clean (2,191 bytes, a standard Drupal robots file, no Claude/Anthropic agent named, nothing relevant disallowed) so we are permitted - but the site itself returned HTTP 403 with a 25-byte body 'Your request was blocked.' That is an edge/WAF rule on our egress, the same datacenter-IP wall PRODUCT_STATUS.md records for NBA.com, KHL, FanGraphs, PFR and Sofascore. HIGH-VALUE RETEST from a GitHub Actions runner: this is the official settlement source for the Clacton by-election and Greater Manchester Mayor markets that are live on the book RIGHT NOW.

FALSE 200 - A SHELL, NOT DATA. The Swedish Election Authority's result portal at https://data.val.se/ returns HTTP 200 but the body is a 2,440-byte Angular SPA skeleton ('<!doctype html><html lang="sv" data-beasties-container>', '<!-- Version: 1.6.2 -->', '<!-- Timestamp: 2026-06-30T14:44:47+0200 -->') with no data in it. Byte-identical 2,440-byte shell returned for /api/valresultat and for a deep 2022 result path - the router serves the same shell for everything, so a status-code check would have scored this as a working source. Its robots.txt is a 404. The underlying api.val.se does not resolve through our proxy ('Tunnel connection failed: 502 Bad Gateway' on CONNECT). NET: no verified free route to official Swedish results, which is the sharpest gap in this file because Sweden's general election is September 2026 and Betwinner has three markets on it live.

REACHABLE BUT THE DATA IS NOT IN THE BODY. europeelects.eu/robots.txt is 'User-agent: * / Disallow:' (allow-all) and pages return real HTML - /data/ is 158,508 bytes, /sweden/ is 188,758 bytes - so this is not a block. But the per-country POLL TABLES are not in the served HTML: /sweden/ contains 'Novus' exactly once (inside an article headline) and ZERO occurrences of 'Demoskop', 'Sifo', 'Ipsos', 'Social Democratic' or 'Sweden Democrats'. The numbers are rendered client-side or embedded from elsewhere. Verified FALSE on coverage, not on reachability - a 200 and 188 KB of bytes bought us nothing. Their upstream dataset (Google Sheet / repository) was not located; that is the thing to chase, not the website.

CLOUDFLARE INTERSTITIAL ON ROBOTS.TXT ITSELF - permission could not even be established, so no content was fetched. https://pollofpolls.eu/robots.txt returned HTTP 403 with a 4,546-byte body whose title is 'Attention Required! | Cloudflare'. When the robots file is unreadable we cannot claim permission, so this is a hard stop rather than a judgement call.

unmodellable: 82 Lottery - RNG BY CONSTRUCTION. Physical ball draws and certified RNG alike. Past draws carry exactly zero information about future ones. The precise reason it is unbeatable is not that we cannot compute the odds - we can compute them EXACTLY from combinatorics - it is that the book can too, prices above the exact fair value, and no information asymmetry is possible. 319 live events, 54 draws, 482 two-way markets in a single MegaMillions draw.

69 Toto - UNMODELLABLE FOR AN UNUSUAL REASON. Not RNG at the top level: it is over/under on the number of correct predictions achieved in Betwinner's OWN parimutuel pool. The decisive input is the joint distribution of what the pool's entrants picked, which the book holds privately and never publishes. Additionally one of the four live draws (Toto Cyber football No.26693) is a simulated-football pool, RNG at its base.

87 Special Bets - n=1 EVENTS WITH NO REFERENCE CLASS. 'Will The Winds of Winter be published', 'Trump to add himself to Mt. Rushmore', 'Sperm Racing Cup 2026'. No base rate, no repeated trial, no data source, no results loop. Mostly bundles of independent props rather than markets. (The Professional Bull Riders is mis-filed here and is a real sport.)

20 TV Games - REAL-WORLD BUT NOT MODELLABLE BY THIS PRODUCT. Awards are juried/voted decisions that are forecastable in principle, but one observation per market per year, no feedback loop, a 20-30% hold, and a genuine information-asymmetry risk (embargoes, pre-recorded formats where the result already exists before the market closes).

303 Games of the Future - MODELLABLE IN PRINCIPLE, BLOCKED ON DATA. A real competition between real athletes, but no free results/standings feed exists (verified negative on both official sites), only 2 markets per match, and hybrid phygital scoring that invalidates borrowed basketball/football priors.

314 Polybet, celebrity/novelty subset - the Obamas-to-divorce class of question is n=1 with no reference class, exactly like sport 87. The macro/financial/crypto subset is NOT in this list and is modellable.
open_questions: WEATHER MARKET SEMANTICS ARE UNRESOLVED and this blocks pricing sportId 176 - the top open item. What is verified: T13117's P encodes an inclusive Celsius band as A.0BB (4.009 = 4-9 C) and T13118's P is a single integer degree, and per airport the two tile the temperature axis contiguously with no gaps (checked independently on Auckland, Sydney, Warsaw, Sheremetyevo, Minsk, Ostrava, Toronto Pearson and Bermuda). What is NOT verified: whether those rows form one exclusive market or a menu of independent one-sided propositions. The feed returns exactly ONE row per (G,GS,P,PL) key - no opposite side - so no overround is computable, and the tiling sums to 2.66-2.77 in implied probability per airport, which is incoherent as an exclusive market. Some listed prices are clearly not live (Bermuda 'exactly 27' at 1.016 = 98.4% implied is impossible for a single degree; every airport's outermost band prices at exactly 5.000, which reads as a cap). This must be settled by reading the rendered market names on the book or its weather rules, and margin_score must not be wired for sport 176 until it is - the difference between a ~20% and a ~170% effective hold decides whether the category is worth surfacing at all.

Does Betwinner settle sportId 176 on METAR, and under what convention? Which station report counts when the market's instant falls between observations, is it the METAR at/nearest the stated UTC time or a SPECI, and how is rounding handled? aviationweather.gov gives integer Celsius and the book's bands are integer Celsius, which lines up suspiciously well - but the book's own weather rules are UNREAD (betwinner.com 302s to betwinner2.com from here, and the rendered rules were not retrieved). Same class of gap as the settlement-terms question PRODUCT_STATUS.md already records.

POLYBET-TO-POLYMARKET MATCH RATE. How many of the 1584 sportId 314 events have an exact Polymarket counterpart, and is Betwinner's 0.80% two-way overround actually a mirrored price plus markup? This is answerable now with a name/semantics matching pass over the verified gamma API. It is worth doing before anything else in this file, because if the match rate is high, the product gains a real reference price - the thing PRODUCT_STATUS.md lists as structurally absent - for an entire category. Guard against false matches: two questions with similar wording and different resolution criteria are worse than no reference.

VERIFY THE 0.80% OVERROUND IS REAL before it touches margin_score. A 0.80% two-way is thinner than anything this project has measured anywhere and thinner than the lottery's 3.1%. Confirm it is a genuine live two-sided price and not a derived/placeholder pair (this feed is known to emit 1.001 placeholders - Toto's outer lines do exactly that). If it is real, sport 314 needs handling outside the standard margin normalisation.

LEGAL, FOR THE OPERATOR: which jurisdictions prohibit betting on elections and political outcomes, and does a tool that SURFACES rather than places such a market carry exposure? The restriction attaches to the subject matter, not only to the operator's licence, so the offshore-book risk already in PRODUCT_STATUS.md does not dispose of it. Recorded, not resolved - the same treatment that document gives jurisdiction. Needs an answer before politics ships to anyone but the operator.

NO VERIFIED FREE ROUTE TO OFFICIAL SWEDISH RESULTS with a live September 2026 market on the book (data.val.se is an SPA shell, api.val.se 502s through our proxy). Same shape for the UK: the Electoral Commission is robots-clean but WAF-403s from our egress with Clacton live in August 2026. Both are prime GitHub Actions retests - that is how this repo already routed around comparable blocks.

CATEGORY OVERLAP - A REAL DEDUP HAZARD IF MORE THAN ONE OF THESE IDS IS INGESTED. Emmy Award 2026 appears under BOTH sportId 20 (tournament 3019358: Outstanding Comedy Series, Drama Series, Lead Actor/Actress) AND sportId 314 (tournament 3030427: Outstanding Supporting Actor/Actress) - the same award is SPLIT across two sport ids with different category sets, so ingesting one gives partial coverage and ingesting both risks double-counting. The same overlap exists for politics: sportId 202 has 'Politics. Brazil' and 'Politics. Canada' and sportId 314 has its own 'Politics. Brazil' and 'Politics. Canada'. The existing dedup on real match id will not catch this because these are genuinely distinct events.

Is there a third-party results source for phygital disciplines (a Liquipedia-style community wiki, or the tournament's live-scoring provider)? Both official sites are verified to carry nothing. Without one, sportId 303 stays unmodelled permanently.

Does the book expose any market for sportId 176 or 314 in the AntePost-style separate sport ids the catalogue uses elsewhere (132, 133, 151)? Not checked; would change the sweep's tournament enumeration.
key_findings: THE MARGIN-RANKING HAZARD - the most operationally important finding here, and it is an engineering one, not a research one. Measured overrounds: Polybet cryptocurrency +0.80%, Lottery +3.10%, Politics +6.7 to +8.3%, Toto +8.1 to +11.7%, Games of the Future +9.0 to +9.3%, TV Games +20 to +30%. Against this project's measured 7.14% median football hold, LOTTERY AND POLYBET ARE THE CHEAPEST MARKETS IN THE ENTIRE BOOK. Because engine/score.py ranks on within-book cheapness, adding sports 82 and 314 to the sweep would put RNG lottery derivatives and mirrored crypto props at the top of every single run - the exact failure CLAUDE.md's HITL check 4 is designed to catch ('if everything is one market type, the filters are wrong'). Sports 82 and 314 must be excluded in config EXPLICITLY, not left to the filters to notice.

TV GAMES IS NOT WHAT THE NAME SUGGESTS, AND THE MISREAD IS THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION. On the 1xBet platform 'TV Games' is also a CASINO vertical of presenter-hosted RNG wheel/keno/bingo titles. LineFeed sportId 20 is a different product entirely: an awards and TV-outright book (Emmy, Oscars, Grammy, Nobel, Hugo, Logie, Strictly, X Factor, Coachella, box office, Spotify Wrapped, Time Person of the Year). Dismissing id 20 as 'RNG casino games' by reflex would have been wrong; so would treating it as modellable. It is real-world and still not worth ranking, for different reasons - 20-30% hold and n=1 events.

GAMES OF THE FUTURE IS REAL - the operator's hypothesis confirmed from two independent sources. Wikipedia: 'an annual global phygital sports tournament, organized by Phygital International'. The 2024 inaugural edition was in Kazan; Betwinner's 2026 events carry MIO.Loc 'SK Qazaqstan (Astana)', corroborated by 20 'Astana' mentions on phygitalinternational.com. Real named club teams (Vozdovac Beograd, MINSK, GTB KZ, Zagrebacki malisani NITUI), real venue, priced at a normal +9.3% like a minor sport. It is NOT a virtual/simulated product and must not be confused with the book's Cyber sports or with Toto Cyber football, which IS simulated.

WEATHER IS THE ONE CATEGORY WORTH BUILDING, and the whole chain is free and verified on both ends - forecast in (api.met.no, 40,066 bytes of hourly air_temperature, robots-clean) and settled observation out (aviationweather.gov METAR, integer Celsius matching the book's integer bands, no robots.txt at all). That observation feed is significant beyond weather: it means sportId 176 is the ONLY thing on the book where we can close a results loop today, and the missing results loop is the P0 hole PRODUCT_STATUS.md names as 'the single biggest architectural hole'. Weather markets are a small, cheap, self-contained place to build the backtest harness against a settling ground truth.

POLITICS IS PRICED LIKE FOOTBALL, NOT LIKE A NOVELTY. Michigan Democratic Primary +6.7%, Clacton by-election +7.0%, Greater Manchester Mayor +8.3% - at or below the book's 7.14% football median, on markets with public polling, prior results, a hard published settlement, and a liquid free reference price. Technically it is the strongest non-weather case in this file. It is held back by law, not by modelling, and by an unverified polling ingest - not by anything about the markets themselves.

POLYBET BREAKS THE PROJECT'S FOUNDING PREMISE. CLAUDE.md opens with 'There is no reference book'. For sportId 314 that is false: Polymarket publishes a free, keyless, liquid price for a large share of these exact questions (verified - 19,259 bytes, outcomePrices already normalised to probabilities, 51 of 60 top-volume markets election-related). Combined with the 0.80% measured overround - a margin no bookmaker sets from its own opinion - the most likely reading is that Betwinner mirrors an external market here at a hair of markup. For this one category the product could make a genuine two-source comparison rather than a within-book cheapness claim. That is a real change in what the tool can honestly say, and it should not be quietly folded into the existing ranking.

THE LOTTERY IS EXACTLY COMPUTABLE AND EXACTLY UNBEATABLE - and the distinction is worth keeping straight. Every derivative market (sum over/under, odd/even counts, ranges) has a closed-form or enumerable true probability. We are not guessing; we KNOW the fair price. That is precisely why there is no edge: the book knows it identically and prices above it, and past draws carry zero information. The one legitimate use follows from the same fact - sport 82 is the only place in the book where the TRUE hold can be measured exactly rather than estimated via proportional de-vig, which makes it a calibration bench for engine/score.py. Never a betting surface.

A DE-VIG TRAP THE ENGINE MUST NOT WALK INTO: this feed BUNDLES independent Yes/No propositions under a single group id and a single event heading. '60 Minutes. Special bets' (7 props) sums to 3.26 implied, 'Netflix Roast. Next Athlete' (50 props) to 3.29, 'Robert Irwin. Special bets' (15 props) to 2.59, 'USA. Congress. Special bets' to 2.15. Those are not 115-229% holds, they are the artefact of adding up unrelated propositions. Critically, GROUP ID ALONE DOES NOT DISTINGUISH THEM - group 9242/3042 carries both a genuine 5-runner exclusive outright (Emmy Lead Actor, +20.0%) and pure bundles. The reliable signal in these categories is the event NAME containing 'Special bets'. Any market whose selections sum far above a plausible hold must be treated as a bundle and excluded from de-vig, not scored.

TOTO IS A BET ON BETWINNER'S OWN POOL, not on football. sportId 69 is 'TOTO total betting results' - over/under (types T12014/T12015, P = 11..15) on the number of correct predictions achieved in a pool draw. The decisive model input is the crowd's entry distribution, which only the book holds. This is a category that looks modellable from the outside (it is football underneath!) and is structurally not.

VERIFICATION-RULE CATCHES, all of which a status-code check would have passed or a robots-blind fetch would have violated: data.val.se returns HTTP 200 with a byte-identical 2,440-byte Angular shell for EVERY path including /api/; europeelects.eu serves 188 KB for /sweden/ containing zero pollster names or party names; pollofpolls.eu returns a Cloudflare interstitial on robots.txt ITSELF, so permission could not be established; electionguide.org names 'User-agent: ClaudeBot / Disallow: /' AND WAF-403s; the UK Electoral Commission is robots-CLEAN but WAF-403s from our egress (a retest target, not a permanent block); en.wikipedia.org's robots.txt itself 403'd once with 'Too many requests' and 200'd minutes later, which is rate-limiting on shared egress and would look like a block in CI. And the headline one: api.open-meteo.com serves 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /' - the canonical free forecast API is robots-disallowed at its API host, as is api.weather.gov, while both brands' documentation sites allow all.
